facts.fact: Civil Registration Services says registration agents (assistant chiefs for home events, health records personnel in facilities) record births on form B1 and deaths on forms D1 or D2, in duplicate, and the Sub-County Registrar signs, stamps and numbers the form to make it the register; it lists manual registration processes as a limitation, and the only digital step it describes is extracting data from the registers into an MS Excel template for monthly statistics.

Civil Registration Services describes the registration of both births and deaths in 2023 as a manual process on paper forms B1, D1 and D2, says the Government seeks to automate the CRS system, and recommends automation of CRS business processes.

Civil Registration Services reports that it operates service delivery points (offices) in 153 of Kenya's 380 sub-counties and describes the registration process at Sub-County Registrars as manual, with paper registers and Excel summaries; it reports no office entering events digitally.

Civil Registration Services, headed by a Secretary, is domiciled in the Ministry of Interior and National Administration, State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services, under Executive Order No. 1 of January 2023, and registers all births and deaths under the Births and Deaths Registration Act.
